How it works

01

Connect your source

Read-only. The tool can't change, create or delete anything.

02

Pick the project and the date

Choose the project that worries you and enter the date you promised, or the one you're about to.

03

Get your number

The chance you hit the date, the realistic date, and how much later or how much scope cutting closes the gap. From 10,000 simulations of your team's real pace.

What is used, and what isn't

Used

  • When an item changed status
  • When it was created and resolved
  • What type of item it is

Not used

  • Titles and descriptions
  • Comments and attachments
  • Who did the work

Your data is only held in memory while the forecast runs. The result is kept 90 days, so you can share it.

Who sees your number? You, and whoever you send the link to.

Your security team wants to check this first? Send them the Method and data page. If they want a walkthrough, it takes about ten minutes. Book that call →

Why a chance and not a date

Same estimate. Days or weeks.

I checked 880 software tasks with the same kind of work, the same estimate and the same process. Half were done within three days. One in twenty took longer than four weeks.

There was no better number to find. Your own history has the chance for every date.

Read the analysis →
Figure: 880 tasks, same estimate. Half done in 3 days, 1 in 20 over 4 weeks.

A low number leaves a question behind: why?

If you can still move the date or cut scope, the card is all you need. Run the Scan again next month and see whether it moved.

If neither can move, the Delivery Audit starts from the same calculation as your Scan and goes after the why: where work waits in your team, what that costs the date, and what to change first. It starts with a free 30 minute call.
